feature: Rename identified speakers from transcript gestures

scenarios.name: Long Mac speaker names remain inside their transcript column
scenarios.given: an actual native Mac transcript row has an identified speaker beside unchanged conversation text
scenarios.when: the speaker name grows from a short label to a long full name
scenarios.then: the actual rendered name changes visibly within its 100-point column without painting any changed pixels beyond that column over the adjacent transcript; the complete name remains in tooltip and accessibility metadata and the original transcript and its layout remain unchanged

scenarios.name: Long press an identified speaker to rename
scenarios.given: an iPhone or iPad transcript contains identified participants
scenarios.when: the reader scrolls an earlier speaker fully into view if necessary, long presses that same speaker, saves a new name, or cancels the editor
scenarios.then: the existing identity is renamed throughout the conversation and in Notes; other speakers remain unchanged and cancellation has no effect; Save and Cancel remain reachable at accessibility text sizes, and a saved name survives rotation; the landscape rename journey uses the actual two-pane workspace with simultaneously visible, nonoverlapping Transcript and Quick panes before editing and after the portrait/landscape roundtrip and Save; no stale speaker Retry control appears in Duo, and the expanded reader after rotation shows exactly two Speaker 1 lines, one renamed Sam line and no Speaker 2 line

manual.reason: Device layout and gesture usability require rendered inspection
steps: Inspect compact, expanded and Duo transcript rename controls with VoiceOver and large text.

scenarios.name: Double click an identified Mac speaker
scenarios.given: a Mac transcript has an identified speaker label
scenarios.when: the user double clicks that label or opens Rename speaker from its menu
scenarios.then: the speaker editor opens for that identity; ordinary single clicks and disabled labels cannot request a rename; live breakdown voices remain nameable before transcript attribution, restored identities update all matching lines, and unknown identities change nothing; delayed finalized lines retain chronological display order, recording identity, capture times and editing identity after renaming; double-clicking transcript words opens only the line editor while double-clicking the speaker label opens only the name sheet, and cancelling that sheet preserves both name and text

manual.reason: Native control tests do not prove the complete installed SwiftUI sheet binding
steps: Double click an identified speaker label in the installed Mac transcript, save a new name, and verify all matching lines and a reopened conversation use it.
Cancel a rename and verify no change; changing conversation while editing must not rename another conversation.

scenarios.name: Cold launch keeps speaker rename ready in the two-pane workspace
scenarios.given: a supported iPhone preview has an isolated synthetic conversation with identified speakers and no-download speaker models already available
scenarios.when: the app launches in portrait, rotates to landscape, and the reader opens and saves the identified speaker rename control
scenarios.then: foreground readiness shows speaker labels on without a stale Retry control before editing or after Save; the actual two-pane workspace has simultaneously visible, nonoverlapping Transcript and Quick panes and a readable transcript viewport, the entire speaker and rename controls are visible, and the expanded reader after Save shows exactly two Speaker 1 lines, one renamed Sam line and no Speaker 2 line; recording never starts
